expected_behavior: runs the SVG lint script first and reports each error and warning with the element it points at
renders the SVG to PNG with the render script (or reports which renderer to install and stops if none exists) and reads the PNG
does the analyze step before judging: transcribes every visible text, counts nodes and edges, then applies the binary checklist
returns a verdict of PASS, FIX (with targeted edits listed), or REDRAW, each finding grounded in something visible
does not edit the file unless asked to fix; when asked, writes a revision next to the original rather than overwriting

cases.prompt: is this mermaid flowchart too busy? (a 26-node flowchart pasted inline)
expected_behavior: runs the mermaid lint and reports node and edge counts against the cap
flags unquoted labels, a lowercase end node, or missing config pin if present
recommends REDRAW with a concrete split (which nodes go to which view) rather than a vague 'simplify'

cases.prompt: check the social card png before I post it
expected_behavior: reads the PNG, transcribes the text, and checks the single takeaway is visible at a glance
notes text that would be unreadable at feed size and contrast that looks low, stated as visible facts
says plainly when a check cannot be done on a raster (no lint possible) and what it did instead

cases.prompt: compare these two visuals and tell me which one is neater
expected_behavior: ranks the candidates rather than assigning absolute scores, and says the ranking is advisory
grounds each ranking reason in a visible fact (crossing edges, label overlap, more than one accent color)
leaves the final pick to the human and never deletes a candidate

reports a fidelity failure of type direction, citing the reversed edge
returns FIX with the exact edge to flip when that is the only mismatch, or REDRAW if more entities are wrong
